meta.label: Video streaming
meta.attribution: Assembled from official pricing pages, terms of service, privacy policies, SEC and other regulatory filings, government and public-library notices, and platform help centers, not measured data. 'Permanence' scores who controls a service's catalog and what that owner has disclosed about pulling licensed or produced content, not whether you personally hold a copy. Every criterion has a cited basis; reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare video streaming by privacy, cost, catalog size, and permanence.

axes.label: Cost or overall fit
axes.question: Lower cost or a stronger overall fit?

axes.label: Catalog size
axes.question: How much choice do you need?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

criteria.label: Permanence (does what you pay for stay there)

products.name: Netflix
products.description: The largest paid subscription service by revenue, with tiers from an ad-supported plan to a 4K Premium plan. Netflix's own SEC filing describes licensed content as available only for a contractual window, so parts of the catalog change over time.

economical.note: Netflix's official pricing page lists Standard with ads at $8.99/month, Standard at $19.99/month and Premium at $26.99/month in the US, with the old ad-free Basic plan discontinued.

privacy.note: Netflix's privacy statement says it collects information about ads viewed and interacted with, device and IP data, and household inferences, and may disclose personal information to 'Advertising Companies' to select and measure ads, while using contractual and technical measures to keep specific title selections from those marketing partners.

permanence.note: Netflix's 2025 Form 10-K says it amortizes licensed and produced content assets 'over the shorter of each title's contractual window of availability, estimated period of use or ten years,' meaning licensed titles are only guaranteed for a fixed window, not permanently.

accessibility.note: Netflix's own help center says it is 'available in over 190 countries and regions' and that its 'library of TV shows and movies varies by country and changes periodically'; it lists China, Crimea, North Korea, Russia and Syria as the places Netflix is not available.

products.name: Amazon Prime Video
products.description: Bundled with an Amazon Prime membership or sold as a standalone ad-supported subscription, with an extra fee for the ad-free Prime Video Ultra tier. The FTC found Amazon used deceptive designs to enroll and retain Prime members, and Amazon's own terms say downloaded and even purchased titles can stop being available.

economical.note: Amazon's official announcement says the standalone Prime Video plan with ads costs $8.99/month, and Prime Video Ultra, the ad-free tier with 4K/Dolby Atmos, costs an extra $4.99/month with no change to the base Prime membership price.

privacy.note: Prime Video's Terms of Use say the service 'may provide Amazon with information relating to your use... including information related to the Digital Content that you download and stream... such as whether and when you viewed the Digital Content,' and that some subscriber viewing history may be shared with content providers in a form 'not identifiable to you' unless authorized.

permanence.note: Prime Video's Terms of Use say Amazon 'may automatically remove Digital Content from your Compatible Device after the end of its Viewing Period,' and that even purchased content 'may become unavailable due to potential content provider licensing restrictions or for other reasons.'

accessibility.note: The FTC's order against Amazon found the company 'enrolled millions of consumers in Prime subscriptions without their consent, and knowingly made it difficult for consumers to cancel,' using 'confusing and deceptive user interfaces'; Amazon paid a $1 billion penalty and $1.5 billion in consumer refunds and must now show a clear button to decline Prime.

products.name: Disney+
products.description: Disney's flagship service, now sold in the US mainly as a bundle with Hulu rather than as a plain standalone plan. Disney's own SEC filing for mid-2023 describes a deliberate removal of produced content from its direct-to-consumer platforms, tied to a $2.4 billion impairment charge.

economical.note: Disney's own plans page lists the cheapest current route to Disney+ in the US as the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99/month with ads, or $19.99/month for the ad-free Bundle Premium; no separate standalone Disney+ price is shown on that page.

privacy.note: California's Attorney General found Disney's opt-out tools only stopped data sharing on the specific device or service used, that its webform did not stop sharing with third-party ad-tech partners, and that Global Privacy Control signals were honored only per device; Disney paid $2.75 million, the largest CCPA penalty to date.

permanence.note: Disney's latest annual report (Form 10-K for fiscal 2025) says 'in fiscal 2023 we announced that we would review content, primarily on our DTC services, for alignment with a strategic change in our approach to content curation, resulting in removal of certain content from our platforms and related impairment charges,' and records a further $109 million of content impairments in fiscal 2025 and $187 million in fiscal 2024.

accessibility.note: Disney's plans page sells Disney+ across several bundle tiers with ads or ad-free, alongside Hulu, ESPN and HBO Max add-ons, indicating broad mainstream distribution through one consumer signup flow.

products.name: HBO Max
products.description: Warner Bros. Discovery's service, renamed from HBO Max to Max and back again, now live in more than 100 markets. The company's own 2022 SEC filing disclosed billions of dollars in content impairment and write-offs after its merger, and Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in October 2026.

economical.note: HBO Max's official help center lists three US plans: Basic with Ads at $10.99/month, Standard at $18.49/month and Premium at $22.99/month, each with a 16% discount for annual billing.

privacy.note: HBO Max's own help page says 'We personalize some ad experiences on HBO Max,' and directs users to the Warner Bros. Discovery Privacy Center to manage ad choices and submit Do Not Sell or Share requests.

permanence.note: Warner Bros. Discovery's Form 8-K says that on October 6, 2026 Skydance Corporation (formerly Paramount Skydance) 'completed the previously announced acquisition' of WBD, which now survives 'as a wholly owned subsidiary,' so HBO Max's catalog has a new owner. WBD's 2025 Form 10-K says its post-merger restructuring included 'strategic content programming assessments,' which its October 2022 Form 8-K had sized at 'approximately $2.0 – $2.5 billion' of 'content impairment and development write-offs,' and it reported a further $203 million of content impairments in 2025.

accessibility.note: Warner Bros. Discovery's own pressroom says HBO Max is 'streaming in over 100 markets worldwide,' with launches in early 2026 covering Italy, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Liechtenstein, Israel and Greece, and further UK and Ireland availability the same year.

products.name: Hulu
products.description: Disney-owned and limited to the United States and its territories. Hulu titles were among those pulled in Disney's 2023 content removal, and Hulu is increasingly sold as part of a Disney+ bundle rather than as a standalone plan.

economical.note: Disney's own site lists the cheapest current route to Hulu in the US as the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99/month with ads, or $19.99/month for the ad-free Bundle Premium.

privacy.note: California's Attorney General settlement covers Disney account opt-out failures 'across all devices and streaming services associated with consumers' Disney accounts,' which includes Hulu as a Disney-owned service; Disney paid $2.75 million to resolve the case.

permanence.note: Disney, which runs Hulu alongside Disney+ in its direct-to-consumer business, says in its latest Form 10-K (fiscal 2025) that 'in fiscal 2023 we announced that we would review content, primarily on our DTC services, for alignment with a strategic change in our approach to content curation, resulting in removal of certain content from our platforms and related impairment charges.'

accessibility.note: Hulu is licensed to stream only within the United States and its territories; it has never offered a normal international signup, which limits who can subscribe at all compared with services sold worldwide.

products.name: Apple TV+
products.description: Apple's original-content subscription, sold on its own or inside Apple One, and included free for a period with some new devices. Apple's own media terms reserve the right to remove content, including purchases, if its distribution rights lapse.

economical.note: Apple's own Apple TV+ page lists the price as $12.99/month after a 7-day free trial, with an Apple One bundle starting at $19.95/month.

privacy.note: Apple's own privacy page for the Apple TV app says it uses 'information about the movies and TV shows you purchase and download to offer advertising' on other Apple surfaces, but also states users 'can choose to turn off Personalized Ads.'

permanence.note: Apple's Media Services Terms and Conditions say 'Content also may be removed from our Services at any time (for instance, because Apple loses its right from the Content provider to make it available), after which it cannot be downloaded, redownloaded, or otherwise accessed from Apple,' and that this can apply even to purchased content.

accessibility.note: Apple's 'Availability of Apple Media Services' support page (published September 30, 2026), which now lists the service as the 'Apple TV subscription,' shows it available in about 168 countries and regions across the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, and notes that Apple TV access 'might be included with your iCloud+ subscription' in some places.

products.name: Paramount+
products.description: Paramount's service carrying CBS, Comedy Central, MTV, Nickelodeon and Showtime titles, sold in dozens of countries. Paramount's own site describes the library only as 'thousands' of episodes and movies rather than giving an exact count.

economical.note: Paramount's own site lists plans starting at $8.99/month for the ad-supported Essential tier, with Premium (ad-free, with Showtime) at $13.99/month.

accessibility.note: Paramount's own site describes the library as 'thousands of full episodes from BET, CBS, Comedy Central, MTV, Nickelodeon, VH1, and more,' and Paramount's global-expansion page describes rolling the service out market by market, including deals in Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, France and South Korea.

products.name: Peacock
products.description: NBCUniversal's service, available only in the United States and its territories. A licensing deal puts a Peacock-branded destination inside Sky's platform in the UK and Europe, but that is Sky content, not a standalone Peacock subscription abroad.

economical.note: Peacock's own help article says Peacock Premium costs '$10.99 a month (+tax) or $109.99 per year (+tax)' and Peacock Premium Plus costs '$16.99 a month (+tax) or $169.99 per year (+tax).'

permanence.note: Comcast's Form 10-K for 2025 says 'Our television networks and Peacock include content licensed from our Studios segment and from third parties,' and that 'We capitalize the costs of licensed content when the license period begins, the content is made available for use and the costs of the licenses are known. Licensed content is amortized as the associated programs are used,' meaning many titles on Peacock are tied to a fixed license period rather than held indefinitely.

accessibility.note: Comcast's own press release describes Peacock content becoming available to 'Sky TV customers and NOW Entertainment Members' as 'a new Peacock destination' inside Sky's existing service, distinct from a direct international Peacock subscription; Peacock itself remains sold only in the US and its territories.

products.name: YouTube
products.description: Free with ads for anyone, with user uploads rather than a licensed studio catalog, plus an optional ad-free Premium tier. Google and YouTube paid a record $170 million to settle FTC and New York allegations that YouTube collected children's data without consent to target ads.

economical.note: YouTube can be watched with ads at no cost; no signup or payment is required to view most public videos.

privacy.note: Google's privacy policy (effective October 1, 2026), which covers YouTube, lists 'Videos you watch' and 'Views and interactions with content and ads' among the activity it collects, uses it to 'recommend a YouTube video you might like,' and says 'we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests and activity across Google services,' with ad controls in My Ad Center.

accessibility.note: YouTube is reachable through a web browser or app with no account required for most viewing, and Google's own privacy policy describes using activity data 'across Google services' including YouTube, indicating broad default access.

products.name: Tubi
products.description: A Fox-owned free ad-supported service with no paid subscription option. Its own privacy policy says that sharing viewing data with advertising partners for targeted ads 'could be considered selling' under some state privacy laws, even though Tubi says it does not sell data as defined under others.

economical.note: Tubi's own corporate site describes itself as a free, ad-supported service with no subscription fee.

privacy.note: Tubi's privacy policy says it collects viewing and search history and uses it 'to deliver and measure more relevant, personalized ads,' and states 'we and our advertising partners use certain Personal Data to deliver online advertisements to you on your devices tailored to your interests, which could be considered "selling" under other state privacy laws,' while saying it does not sell data as defined under Virginia's law.

accessibility.note: Tubi's own corporate page says it is available in the US, Canada, Mexico, LATAM, the United Kingdom and Australia, and can be accessed on 'over 30 devices.'

products.name: Pluto TV
products.description: A free, ad-supported live-channel and on-demand service owned by Paramount. Paramount's own press page calls it 'a global leader in free streaming television,' built on partnerships with hundreds of media companies rather than a paid catalog.

economical.note: Pluto TV's own site describes itself as letting people 'Watch 1000s of free movies and TV shows on demand & 100s of live TV channels for free,' with no subscription fee.

catalog.note: Pluto TV's own site says it offers '1000s of free movies and TV shows on demand & 100s of live TV channels,' a broad but imprecise figure compared with services that publish an exact title count.

accessibility.note: Paramount's own press page describes Pluto TV as 'the leading free streaming television service' and 'a global leader in free streaming television,' built in partnership with 'over 425 international media companies.'

products.name: Plex
products.description: A free ad-supported film and TV library plus a self-hosted media server for files you already own. Plex's own privacy policy says it will not collect or sell information about titles in a personal media library, while it does share some account data for advertising on the free streaming side.

economical.note: Plex's own free-movies page says its on-demand movies and shows are '100% Free' and fully licensed, with no credit card required, and the Plex Media Server software is also free to run.

privacy.note: Plex's March 2025 privacy policy states 'We do not and will not collect information about content or titles in your personal media library or what you've played,' and for personal media users specifically, 'we do NOT, and will not, share or sell any information about the content and titles on or your use of a personal media server,' while separately listing hashed emails and online identifiers as data shared with advertisers for the ad-supported streaming side.

catalog.note: Plex's own free-movies page says it offers 'Stream 50K+ titles on demand' plus '600+ channels' of free live TV.

permanence.note: Plex's Terms of Service for the Plex Media Server say the software may only be used on 'a device or hardware that you own' and that 'Content available on your PMS Software must be on storage that you own,' meaning the self-hosted side of Plex is explicitly built around content you already control.

accessibility.note: The free streaming catalog requires no payment and no account beyond signup, while running a personal Plex Media Server requires setting up and maintaining your own hardware, a materially higher effort than opening an app.

products.name: Kanopy
products.description: A film library available at no direct cost through a participating public library card, funded by the library rather than by a subscription or ads. Access is rationed by a monthly ticket allowance rather than by price.

economical.note: The San Francisco Public Library's own FAQ says Kanopy 'is free to San Francisco Public Library cardholders,' with the library paying for access on the cardholder's behalf.

catalog.note: The San Francisco Public Library's own FAQ describes Kanopy as providing access to 'more than 30,000 independent and documentary films,' including Criterion Collection and Great Courses titles.

accessibility.note: The San Francisco Public Library's own FAQ says a valid library card and PIN are required, and that cardholders 'receive 30 tickets to use every month,' with most titles costing a minimum of 2 tickets and unused tickets not carrying over.

products.name: Criterion Channel
products.description: The Criterion Collection's own hand-picked subscription, limited to the United States and Canada, built around a rotating library of about 2,000 films plus shorts and supplements rather than a broad mainstream catalog.

economical.note: Criterion's own FAQ says 'A monthly subscription to the Criterion Channel costs $10.99 USD a month and an annual subscription costs $99.99 USD a year,' with a free 7-day trial.

catalog.note: Criterion's own FAQ says subscribers 'can browse and filter the 2000+ films available to stream,' along with 'more than 500 shorts and 5,000 supplementary features.'

accessibility.note: Criterion's own FAQ says 'The Criterion Channel is available only in the U.S. and Canada,' with no wider international launch yet, and there is no free ad-supported tier.

products.name: Mubi
products.description: A hand-picked subscription built around a daily rotation: films are added to the main selection and depart on a schedule, with Mubi's own help center flagging departures roughly two weeks ahead.

economical.note: Mubi's own membership page lists the standard MUBI plan at $14.99/month or $119.88/year, with a pricier MUBI GO tier at $19.99/month that adds a weekly cinema ticket in select cities.

permanence.note: Mubi's own help center says 'we will always label films that are leaving the platform within the next 14 days,' confirming that films are only available on Mubi for a limited, rotating window rather than staying indefinitely.

accessibility.note: Mubi's own membership page and App Store listing note that content and pricing vary by country but do not give a full list of served countries; the base subscription is sold with no free ad-supported tier.

products.name: Internet Archive (public domain and open film collections)
products.description: The nonprofit Internet Archive's public-domain and openly licensed film collections, free to stream or download with no purchase. The Archive says it does not charge for access, sell user data, or run ads.

economical.note: The Internet Archive's own site states it does not 'charge for access, sell user information, or run ads,' and is 'powered by online donations' rather than fees.

privacy.note: The Internet Archive's own privacy statement says it does not 'charge for access, sell user information, or run ads,' and separately says of donor data, 'We do not sell or trade your information with anyone.'

catalog.note: The Archive's 'Public Domain Movies' collection page lists 385 files totalling 971.6GB in this single named collection; the Archive hosts several other separate film collections beyond this one, so this figure describes one collection rather than the whole site.

permanence.note: The Archive describes itself as an independent nonprofit funded by donations rather than ad revenue or licensing deals, and its film holdings are public domain or rights-cleared for redistribution, so titles are not subject to the kind of licensing-window removal that Netflix, Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery disclose in their own filings.

accessibility.note: The Public Domain Movies collection page is titled 'Free Download, Borrow, and Streaming,' and offers multiple downloadable formats without a purchase or subscription.

products.name: The Roku Channel
products.description: Roku's free, ad-supported service of on-demand titles and live channels, with paid add-on subscriptions billed through Roku. It runs on Roku devices in the US, UK, Canada and Mexico and on other platforms in the US. In 2025 Michigan's Attorney General sued Roku, alleging it collected children's personal information without parental consent.

economical.note: Roku's own Roku Channel page offers thousands of free TV shows and movies, Roku Originals and more than 500 live TV channels with a free account; the paid Premium Subscriptions it sells alongside them are optional add-ons.

privacy.note: Roku's privacy policy (last updated July 1, 2026) says it uses information 'to show you ads (including personalized ads) through the Roku Services, on Third-Party Channels, and on third-party websites' and links the devices of one person or household 'for purposes of advertising to that individual or household on different browsers or devices'. Even with automatic content recognition switched off, 'Roku still receives information about your interactions and streaming activities on your devices through other methods'. Sharing which specific titles you watch with third parties for ads requires opting in to a 'Content Viewing Disclosure' setting.

catalog.note: Roku's Form 10-K for 2025 says that on The Roku Channel 'Viewers can stream a broad variety of 80,000+ movies and TV shows, including Roku Originals, for free', plus more than 500 free ad-supported live channels.

permanence.note: Roku's Form 10-K for 2025 says 'The foundation of our content strategy for The Roku Channel is third-party licensed content and, to a smaller extent, our original programming, Roku Originals', so most of the catalog is held on licence rather than owned.

accessibility.note: Roku's Form 10-K for 2025 says 'The Roku Channel is available on devices powered by the Roku TV OS in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Mexico', and that in the US it is also available through the Roku mobile app, on the web and on Amazon Fire TV, Samsung, Google TV and other Android TV devices. No payment is needed for the free tier.

products.name: YouTube TV
products.description: Google's live TV subscription, with national and local networks, a cloud DVR and up to six household accounts. It is sold only in the United States and costs far more than an on-demand subscription.

economical.note: YouTube TV's own site says 'YouTube TV is $82.99/mo for 1 membership with up to 6 household accounts', and lists a smaller Sports + News plan at $71.99/mo after an introductory discount. That is several times the price of the cheapest on-demand plans in this lens.

privacy.note: Google's privacy policy (effective October 1, 2026), which covers YouTube services, lists 'Videos you watch' and 'Views and interactions with content and ads' among the activity it collects, and says 'we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests and activity across Google services', with ad controls in My Ad Center.

accessibility.note: YouTube TV's own site says 'YouTube TV is available nationwide in over 99.5% of households in the United States' and that members can cancel at any time: 'There are no fees for canceling'. It is not sold outside the US, and it does not refund partial billing periods.

products.name: AMC+
products.description: A subscription bundle of AMC, BBC America, IFC and SundanceTV programming that also includes Shudder, Sundance Now and IFC Films Unlimited. Its owner, AMC Networks, renamed itself AMC Global Media in April 2026, and its annual report records write-offs of programming it no longer uses.

economical.note: AMC+'s own site lists Monthly with Ads at $7.99/month, ad-free Monthly Premium at $10.99/month and Annual Premium at $109.99/year, each with a 7-day free trial.

privacy.note: AMC Global Media's streaming privacy policy (effective June 27, 2025), which covers AMC+, lists 'Content viewing patterns' and 'browsing activities, title selections, and search queries' among the data it collects. It gives residents of US states with privacy laws a right to opt out of 'sale', sharing for cross-context behavioural advertising and targeted advertising, which means these uses are on unless you opt out.

permanence.note: AMC Networks' Form 10-K for 2025 says 'We have incurred write-offs of program rights in the past, including $64.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 and $7.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2025', and may write off more 'if it is determined that program rights have limited, or no, future usefulness'. AMC's separate streaming terms of use also reserve the right to add, remove or disable access to content at its sole discretion.

accessibility.note: AMC Networks' Form 10-K for 2025 says 'We have launched several of our services, most notably AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder and HIDIVE, in select international markets, including Canada, parts of Europe, Australia and New Zealand', so AMC+ is mainly a US service with limited reach abroad. There is no free tier.

products.name: Starz
products.description: A premium US subscription of original series and films, now an independent company after separating from Lionsgate. Its own filing says that before the split it removed programming from the Starz platform and wrote it off.

economical.note: Starz's own signup page offers a discounted first three months but says the service then rolls to month-to-month at the current price of $11.99/month, or $69.99/year paid annually.

privacy.note: Starz's privacy notice (effective June 23, 2026) says it collects viewing information, including the titles and genres you watch and your searches. It shares personal information with advertising partners to build lookalike audiences and says it sells or shares information for targeted advertising unless you opt out. For Rhode Island residents it names Amazon, Facebook, Google, Rokt and Snapchat as third parties that may receive such data.

permanence.note: Starz's transition report on Form 10-KT (period to December 31, 2025) says that before its separation from Lionsgate it 'identified certain other programming with limited strategic purpose, which was removed from the Starz Platform and abandoned by the Company'. It recorded content impairment charges of $213.0 million and $156.4 million in the fiscal years to March 2024 and March 2025, plus $6.8 million in the nine months to December 2025.

accessibility.note: Starz's Form 10-KT says 'Starz is a leading provider of premium subscription video programming to consumers in the U.S.', with 17.63 million US subscribers at December 31, 2025, sold directly and through distributors. In October 2025 it moved Canada to a licensing arrangement run by a partner. There is no free tier.

products.name: Curiosity Stream
products.description: An ad-free documentary and factual subscription founded by Discovery Channel founder John Hendricks. Its annual report says about three quarters of its titles are licensed, many of those licences expire in 2026 and 2027, and the company also licenses its library for AI model training.

economical.note: Curiosity Stream's own site lists the Standard plan at $5.99/month, or $4.17/month when billed annually, with a Smart Bundle of five services at $11.99/month.

privacy.note: Curiosity Stream's privacy policy says 'We may sell or share identifiers, commercial information, internet or other electronic network activity information' and other categories of personal information, with an opt-out from sale or sharing for targeted advertising. The streaming service itself carries no ads.

catalog.note: CuriosityStream's Form 10-K for 2025 describes its library as 'approximately 14,000 programs' in the business overview but as 'approximately 6,000 programs' in the results section. Either way it is a mid-sized, documentary-only catalog.

permanence.note: CuriosityStream's Form 10-K for 2025 says 'a significant portion of our content is subject to license for a given period', and that 'approximately 75% of the titles on our CuriosityStream SVOD service were subject to licenses, approximately 18% of which expire in 2026 and approximately 17% of which expire in 2027'.

accessibility.note: Curiosity Stream's help center (updated January 2026) says the service is available worldwide in all countries and can be paid for with major credit or debit cards. Content varies by country because some acquired titles are geo-blocked, but its own originals are available everywhere.

products.name: BBC iPlayer
products.description: The BBC's on-demand and live TV service in the UK. It carries no adverts there, but you need a TV licence to use it, and most programmes stay up for a set window after broadcast rather than permanently. It works only from inside the UK.

economical.note: The UK government's Department for Culture, Media and Sport says 'The annual cost of a TV licence will rise to £180 from 1 April 2026', about £15 a month, which is the price of using BBC iPlayer. Free licences remain for over-75s on Pension Credit, and blind people and care-home residents pay reduced fees.

privacy.note: The BBC's privacy policy says personalisation is switched on by default when you create a BBC account (it is off for under-13s), and that it uses your information to check whether you use BBC iPlayer and to keep the TV licensing database up to date. For its own marketing on Facebook, Google, Snapchat and Twitter it says 'we will share your data in a hashed format with these providers'. It shows advertising only when you use BBC services from outside the UK.

permanence.note: BBC iPlayer's own help page says 'much of our content is available for 30 days after broadcast', with some current affairs kept for 365 days, news bulletins for as little as 24 hours, and some programmes removed for editorial or legal reasons. It adds that 'we always try to make programmes available as long as our rights allow' and that it cannot extend a programme on request.

accessibility.note: BBC iPlayer's own help page says 'A valid TV Licence is required to watch or download any programmes on BBC iPlayer' on any device, and that watching without one is a criminal offence with fines of up to £1,000. A separate iPlayer help page says you must be in the UK to stream or download.

products.name: ITVX
products.description: ITV's streaming service for the UK: free with adverts, with a paid Premium tier that adds BritBox content and removes most ads. In July 2026 ITV agreed to sell the business that runs ITVX to Sky, subject to regulatory approval and expected to complete in the second half of 2027.

economical.note: ITVX's terms of use say content is offered 'without payment, on an ad-supported but free-to-use basis' through the Standard Service, with a paid Premium Service for extra content and fewer adverts.

privacy.note: ITV's privacy notice says it collects 'viewing and browsing history' and that 'Most ITV services are funded by advertising products and services, which include some targeted advertising products'. It shares registration and usage data with ad partners and sends hashed email IDs to platforms such as Facebook and Google for marketing. Users can limit this through a Data Permissions setting and opt out of targeted ads.

permanence.note: ITVX's terms of use say 'All Content is subject to change and is variable from time to time' and that ITV may 'remove and/or alter the Content available via the Service and/or the functionality of the Service at any time and for any reason whatsoever'.

accessibility.note: ITVX's terms of use limit registration to people aged 16 or over in 'the United Kingdom, Channel Islands or Isle of Man' and say the service uses geo-blocking outside that territory. The standard tier is free once you register.

products.name: Channel 4 streaming
products.description: The publicly owned, advertising-funded broadcaster's free streaming service (formerly All 4), with a paid Channel 4+ tier that removes most adverts. It is available only in the UK and Republic of Ireland.

economical.note: Channel 4's terms of use say 'most of our Content is available to you for free' and is funded by selling advertising around it; the paid Channel 4+ tier is optional.

privacy.note: Channel 4's privacy policy says it collects 'Behavioural Data', including viewing history and the ads you have been shown, to tailor ads and recommendations. Through 'data pairing' it enriches registered users' data with information from third-party providers such as Acxiom, and it can personalise ads with your name, gender, location or birth month. These are on unless you opt out in Privacy settings. It does not serve targeted ads to registered users under 18.

permanence.note: The Channel 4+ terms (updated 9 December 2024) say content availability 'may change from time to time' when 'third party rights-holders withdraw, restrict or place obligations on our right to use that content', and that Channel 4 can 'add or withdraw or change Channel 4 Content at any time, with or without notice'.

accessibility.note: Channel 4's own FAQ says 'Channel 4 streaming is only available in the UK and Republic of Ireland'. Its terms of use require registered users to be 16 or over, and the ad-supported tier is free.

products.name: hoopla
products.description: A digital lending service offered free through participating public libraries. It lends films and TV episodes alongside ebooks, audiobooks and music, with a monthly borrowing cap that each library sets.

economical.note: Delaware's public libraries describe hoopla as a free service: you sign in with a Delaware library card to borrow movies, TV shows, music, ebooks and audiobooks, and the library pays.

accessibility.note: Chicago Public Library's FAQ says 'You can check out 5 hoopla titles every calendar month', that 'one episode of a TV show counts as one checkout', and that movies and TV are lent for 3 days. Delaware's libraries allow 4 borrows a month. A library card from a participating library is required.

products.name: Nebula
products.description: A creator-owned, ad-free subscription for independent video creators' originals, bonus cuts and early releases. Nebula says profits are split 50/50 between its creators and the company.

economical.note: Nebula's own site lists the subscription at $6/month or $60/year, unlimited and ad-free.

privacy.note: Nebula's privacy policy says Nebula, its service providers and advertising partners may automatically log your activity on and off its services. It uses session-replay tools that record clicks, scrolls and typing, and it may share hashed customer lists with advertising and social media companies to advertise Nebula to you and to similar users. The service itself shows no ads.

permanence.note: Nebula's terms of service say subscribers may stream content during the paid period but that Nebula 'may add or remove Content from the Platform at any time'. Lifetime plans cover the content types available at purchase 'for as long as the Platform is available and supported'.

accessibility.note: Nebula's FAQ lists apps for iOS, tvOS, Android, Android TV, Fire TV, Roku, Samsung and LG TVs, but says LG removed the Nebula app from its stores in 46 countries in November 2023 because Nebula carries LGBTQ+ content. Its terms bar signups only from countries under comprehensive US sanctions. There is no free tier.
